column1: # China NGCC round-1 signature instances. Columns: see bench-common/ngcc/gen_rules.py.
# One row per ALGORITHM_INSTANCE. Explain non-obvious srcs/defs/patches in a comment line above the row.

# status.tsv was produced per group of 5 candidates inside the container (a single full status run is killed by memory pressure), KAT records checked against bench-common/ngcc/kat_hashes.tsv. NGCC_KAT_TIMEOUT: 900 s; sign-12 Galas-384S/F (rerun alone): 2400 s; rows that timed out at 300-600 s in the previous run were re-checked at 60 s. Rows changed by the 2026-10-08 build-file audit batch (submitters' Makefile/CMake defines, DOVE mapping) were rebuilt and re-checked per candidate group at 900 s. A TIMEOUT row exceeded its limit.

# iters: every buildable row is explicit. Measured rows: 1000, or about 30 s of timed work (rows changed by the 2026-10-08 audit batch re-measured with BENCH_ITER=3 in the container) (floor 10; 5 above 60 s per iteration; TRINE-512-* and UVW-512 are set to 1/1/2 because one pass took over 25 min in the container). Rows that never complete a timed bench pass keep a conservative 10 and have no timings: Tins128/256/512 and UVW-128/256 fail the warm-up checks (valid signature rejected / tampered signature accepted); Origami-128 and Origami-512 fail the warm-up only intermittently (sig_sign returns -4 in about 6.5% of keygen+sign loops at 128, 5/100 at 512: container loop, 2026-10-08); SQIsign2D-lvl2 (SIGFPE) aborts with random keys (the SQISign2Dsquare rows no longer abort since they build with the Makefile's -DNDEBUG -DSQISIGN_FP2_ASM_P<q>); the bench now records them as DNF rows and continues (see bench/CLAUDE.md, Crash isolation and DNF rows). Tins256 also fails a warm-up check (tampered signature accepted).
# Aigis-Sig+: aigis_sig.c is the vendor speed-test main (needs speed.c/cpucycles.c). randombytes.c reads /dev/urandom; rng.c already routes randombytes() to drng_algorithm, so drop it.

# Parameter set: -DPARAMS=1|2|3 (params.h has no default). KDF: -DUSE_ICCS is the only choice that reproduces the submitted KAT (USE_SM3 and USE_SHA3 give MISMATCH); it routes XOF/hash through the ICCS placeholders pseudoXOF/pseudohash, which status.tsv records as hash=placeholder.
# SM3 comes from the bundled ippcpsm3/ subdirectory, which '*' does not descend into; patches/sign-01/sm3_block.c compiles its UpdateSM3 block function (never included by a .c file upstream).

# Optimised x86 (avx2/ subtree): the AVX2 sources use USE_ICCS like the reference build and need keccak4x/KeccakP-1600-times4-SIMD256.c; the SM3 sources are not used (placeholder hash); aes.c (needs a missing aes.h) and randombytes.c are dropped, rng.c routes randombytes() to drng_algorithm.
# sign-02 BiT-384: not built: the archive has no BiT-384 implementation (only 128/256/512); its claims row comes from the specification.

# Optimised x86 (BiT-<n>-avx2): consts.c is compiled through patches/sign-02/wrap_consts.c (hidden visibility, so the PC-relative asm references link into a shared object). -DASM_ALIASES as in each Makefile (BiT-128 needs it: the .S files define the ntt_avx_* names only then; no effect in 256/512); BiT-256 drops shuffle.S, a leftover that uses an undefined cdecl() macro.

# CEDRUSC, CEDRUSALPHA (sign-04), Flextree (sign-11), sign-17: sign.c defines the NIST-API crypto_sign_* symbols that the shim also exports; the candidate's copies are renamed with -D (defs never reach the shim). Instances whose KAT replay is slow use katn 2 (slow KAT replay).
# Optimised x86 (SM3x8 hashing): same flags as the reference build.

# sm4th/ublockith/vistrutith: the instance header is <instance>_AlgorithmInstance.h; <instance>_bench.c and <instance>_test.c (vistrutith) and field_mul_bench.c (ublockith_d3_256s) are mains; utils_* subdirectories hold the primitives ('*' does not descend). The 'tight' and ublock instances need -DUSE_BALLET=1 -DHAVE_BALLET_CORE=1.

# Optimised x86: defines from each instance's Makefile defaults (NDEBUG ?= 1, *_FIELD_PCLMUL ?= 1, USE_SBOX_TABLE, PRG_ACCE ?= 1 with SM4 or AES-NI acceleration, HYGON_SM4_ACCE ?= 0): sm4th loose -DNDEBUG -DSM4TH_FIELD_PCLMUL -DSBOX_TABLE -DSM4_SBOX_TABLE -DPRG_ACCE=1 -DSM4TH_ENABLE_SM4_ACCE=1 -DSM4TH_ENABLE_HYGON_CIS=0 (no hygon_cis_sm4*.{c,S}); sm4th tight the same plus Ballet, and utils_sm4/sm4_asm.S; ublockith -DNDEBUG -DUBLOCKITH_FIELD_PCLMUL -DPRG_ACCE=1 -DUBLOCKITH_ENABLE_SM4_ACCE=0; vistrutith -DNDEBUG -DVISTRUTITH_FIELD_PCLMUL -DPRG_ACCE=1 -DVISTRUTITH_ENABLE_AESNI=1 -DVISTRUTITH_FAEST_AVX_SBOX=1 -DVISTRUTITH_ASSUME_AESNI=1. Without them the rows ran the portable code (vistrutith 500-900x slower, KAT replay TIMEOUT).

# sign-09 DOVE: the implementations are nested .rar archives, unpacked only in the container (bench-common/ngcc/unpack_nested.py, then extract.py --import-unpacked). Both .rar packages hold the same 4 ICCS trees (DOVE_{classic,pkc_skc}_{ref,avx2}, ALGORITHM_INSTANCE "dove" in all); the parameter set is chosen by -DDOVE_PARAM_SET=DOVE128|256|512 (Makefile DOVE_PARAM). # Facto-DSA-512: no submitted KAT file exists (kat '-'), so status is NOKAT.

MISMATCH is expected: the submitted KATs come from a non-ICCS generator that uses galas_set_kat_seed, while the ICCS keygen ignores drng_algorithm (fixed key pair). column1: # GreatWall: rng.c is broken upstream (unterminated comment) and unused (randomness comes from randomness_randombytes.c via drng_algorithm); api.c defines NIST-API symbols that clash with the shim, so they are renamed.

# Optimised x86: same flags as the reference build; every row drops the files its Makefile does not build (mq.c, rain*.c, the other levels' greatwall-*-matrix.c). GreatWall512f/512s: the submitted optimised tree crashes (SIGSEGV in prg_tree_gen) because the SECURITY_PARAM == 512 PRG copies 32-byte-aligned block512 keys into a malloc() buffer (docs/ngcc-submission-bugs.md U10); patches/sign-13/prgs.h allocates it with aligned_alloc and is compiled into prgs.c, small_vole.c, vector_com.c and vole_commit.c through the wrap_*.c files (via the unmodified copy patches/sign-13/vole_params.h). KAT PASS, sizes identical to the reference build.

# Lynxer, ReSolveD-alpha (sign-21): -DXOF_PSEUDO is the submitter's Makefile default (pseudoXOF from auxfunc.c, which routes through the ICCS placeholders); the SHAKE XOF would need the sha3/ sources, so none are built. Instances whose KAT replay is slow use katn 2 (slow KAT replay).

# lwrdsa: sig_sign writes a detached signature of CRYPTO_BYTES bytes but reports CRYPTO_BYTES+mlen (heap over-read in callers; docs/ngcc-submission-bugs.md item 2). patches/sign-15/SIG_lwrdsa<n>.c is the wrapper with *sn_len_bytes = CRYPTO_BYTES and nothing else changed, so we benchmark a patched wrapper. The submitted KAT Sn records are CRYPTO_BYTES+mlen long and end in leaked heap bytes, so the generic KAT compare reports MISMATCH (expected; the benchmark sizes use the detached CRYPTO_BYTES).
# Octarine: the ICCS API is in sign.c with sign.h as instance header; sign_test.c is a test copy of the getters and is dropped. Sources in arith/ and utils/ are listed explicitly.
# Optimised x86: AVX2 assembly in arith/ is listed explicitly; -DRRLWR_SECURITY_LEVEL=<n> is required (also for the shim, which includes parameters.h).

# Octarine: -DRRLWR_SECURITY_LEVEL=<n> is inferred from the sources (the submitter's Makefile is not extracted); the optimised parameters.h has no default and #errors without it, whereas the reference tree defaults to 128.

# Origami: the submitted KAT files hold a single record, so katn is 1. sig_sign returns -4 in about 7% of calls (docs/ngcc-submission-bugs.md item 16); patches/sign-18/SIG_AlgorithmInstance.c retries inside sig_sign with a fresh salt from drng_algorithm, as the submitter's own Common/bench_sig.c (sign_with_retry, limit 10000) does. The first attempt is unchanged, so KAT PASS.
# Optimised x86 (origami_opt.c instead of origami_ref.c): same flags as the reference build plus -DORIGAMI_OPT=OPT from the Makefile (symbol prefix only).

# Phoenix: -DPARAMS=<lower-case instance> picks params/params-<instance>.h; -DSUBMISSION_DRNG routes randombytes through drng_algorithm (the default reads /dev/urandom) and -DALLOW_DEEP_TREES is needed by the larger sets. The SM3 variants contain both wots*.c and gwots*.c (same symbols; sign.c uses gwots), so wots.c and wotsx1.c are dropped. The SHAKE instances use patches/sign-19/drng.c (the ICCS SM3 DRNG): the submitted SHAKE KATs were generated with it. Phoenix-SM3 still MISMATCHES: cause unknown; not reproducible from the ref or avx2 code. NIST-API symbols are renamed as in sign-03.

# Phoenix-SHAKE optimised x86 (avx2/ subtree): its parameter headers define SPX_BYTES without the 2-byte TFORS length field (docs/ngcc-submission-bugs.md item 3), so CRYPTO_BYTES was 2 B below the maximum signature length; patches/sign-19/SIG_AlgorithmInstance_shake_avx2.c (the only user of CRYPTO_BYTES) redefines it as SPX_BYTES + 2, and the rows also use patches/sign-19/drng.c and -DAVX2_OPTIMIZED from the Makefile. 192s, 256f, 384s, 384f, 512s, 512f: KAT PASS, sizes identical to the reference build. 192f (different SPX_TFORS_SIG_MAX, 30790 vs 30766 B) and 256s (KAT MISMATCH) stay on the reference build.
# QingLuan: sources in api_pkc/ (ICCS adapters) and src/; the adapters replace src/hash.c and src/utils.c, so those two are dropped. Level macro -DQINGLUAN_<n>.

column1: # Sigurd stays on the reference build: the optimised tree creates worker threads (pthread_create in sig_core.c, -pthread), which a per-thread cycle counter does not see; the reference tree is single-threaded.
# SQISign2Dsquare: instance root is the parent of sqisign/; uses system GMP (-lgmp, not the bundled gmp.h). A compressed and an uncompressed KAT exist; see the kat column. katn 1 (slow KAT replay).

# Optimised x86: the field arithmetic assembly (ec_arithmetic/fp_p<q>_asm.S, fp2_p<q>_asm.S) is listed explicitly; -DNDEBUG (release build, sqisign/Makefile:38) and -DSQISIGN_FP2_ASM_P<q> (:47) as in the Makefile; without the latter fp2.c never calls the assembly and sign.c takes the slower theta-chain strategy whose assertion aborts with random keys.

column1: # Tins: the instance header is SIG_TINS<n>.h. Tins128 CRYPTOFAIL (sig_verify rejected) under our global -O3 -march=native; it passes at the submitter's -O2. Writing the recomputed hash to test_h_piop (item 7) is not enough to fix it, so Tins128 has no patch. Tins512: sig_verify copied the uninitialised aux buffer over the signature instead of reading it (docs/ngcc-submission-bugs.md item 7); patches/sign-29/SIG_TINS512.c reverses that memcpy: KAT PASS, but like Tins256 the warm-up check still fails (tampered signature accepted, item 14). We keep the global flags (per-row cflags are parked). katn 1 (slow KAT replay).
# Optimised x86 for Tins256 only (Tins128/Tins512 stay on the reference build: CRYPTOFAIL in both optimised builds).

# TRINE: exactly one of USE_SHA3/USE_ICCS must be defined and USE_ICCS (placeholder hash) is used; patches/sign-30/api.h declares the NIST-API symbols under their renamed (cand_*) names so the shim's own prototypes do not clash. Keys and signatures are megabytes, so katn is 1-2 (megabyte keys and signatures make replay slow).
# Optimised x86 (Performance_Optimized_Implementation): same flags as the reference build.

# UVW: -DUSE_API_PKC selects the ICCS hash glue. Keys are huge (UVW-512 pk is 95 MB; ngcc_kat cap raised to 256 MiB; UVW-256 and UVW-512 still TIMEOUT at 600 s because key generation is that slow), katn 1 (huge keys: one record is enough and keeps memory bounded).
# Optimised x86 for UVW-128 only (UVW-256/512 stay on the reference build: KAT replay TIMEOUT in both).
# VDOO: -DVDOO_<n> selects the set; vdoo-*.c are alternate copies of the vdoo_*.c files (dropped); api.c is renamed as in sign-03. VDOO-512 katn 1 (slow KAT replay).
# yuanyang: drng_algorithm.c defines drng_algorithm itself (-DNGCC_NO_DRNG for the shim); the ntrugen key generator lives under keygen/.

# Optimised x86 (yuanyang-1024/2048 only; the yuanyang-512 optimised build MISMATCHes, also with -DYUANYANG_HAVE_AVX2_IMPL=1 (the submitter builds it with -Ofast, which we do not use); the reference build passes): -DYUANYANG_HAVE_AVX2_IMPL=1 as in the Makefile (otherwise the AVX2 NTT is compiled but never called); -DYUANYANG_FORCE_SOFTWARE_RANDOMNESS takes randomness from the ICCS DRNG callback instead of /dev/urandom; the shared cpu_features.c and the headers sysrng.h/cpu_features.h live one directory above the instance directory upstream, so unmodified copies are in patches/sign-34.
